params._orderID: The order to lookup the details of. Can be the ID of a        buy or a sell order.

getMatchDetails(bytes32).return: [     a boolean representing whether or not the order has been settled,     a boolean representing whether or not the order is a buy     the 32-byte order ID of the matched order     the volume of the priority token,     the volume of the secondary token,     the fee paid in the priority token,     the fee paid in the secondary token,     the token code of the priority token,     the token code of the secondary token ]

renounceOwnership().details: Allows the current owner to relinquish control of the contract.

params._buyID: The 32 byte ID of the buy order.
params._sellID: The 32 byte ID of the sell order.

params._guiltyOrderID: The 32 byte ID of the order of the guilty trader.

params._minimumVolume: The minimum volume the trader is willing to        accept. Encoded the same as the volume.
params._prefix: The miscellaneous details of the order required for        calculating the order id.
params._price: The price of the order. Interpreted as the cost for 1        standard unit of the non-priority token, in 1e12 (i.e.        PRICE_OFFSET) units of the priority token).
params._tokens: The encoding of the token pair (buy token is encoded as        the first 32 bytes and sell token is encoded as the last 32        bytes).
params._volume: The volume of the order. Interpreted as the maximum        number of 1e-12 (i.e. VOLUME_OFFSET) units of the non-priority        token that can be traded by this order.

getMatchDetails(bytes32).notice: Retrieves the settlement details of an order. For atomic swaps, it returns the full volumes, not the settled fees.

hashOrder(bytes,uint64,uint64,uint256,ui.notice: Exposes the hashOrder function for computing a hash of an order's details. An order hash is used as its ID. See `submitOrder` for the parameter descriptions.

renounceOwnership().notice: Renouncing to ownership will leave the contract without an owner. It will not be possible to call the functions with the `onlyOwner` modifier anymore.

settle(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Settles two orders that are matched. `submitOrder` must have been called for each order before this function is called.

slash(bytes32).notice: Slashes the bond of a guilty trader. This is called when an atomic swap is not executed successfully. To open an atomic order, a trader must have a balance equivalent to 0.6% of the trade in the Ethereum-based token. 0.2% is always paid in darknode fees when the order is matched. If the remaining amount is is slashed, it is distributed as follows:   1) 0.2% goes to the other trader, covering their fee   2) 0.2% goes to the slasher address Only one order in a match can be slashed.

submitOrder(bytes,uint64,uint64,uint256,.notice: Stores the details of an order.
